overview: The Ouray–Red Mountain Toll Road was a major wagon-road and stage corridor built through the San Juan mining country under the transportation network associated with Otto Mears.

Construction proceeded in stages during the early 1880s; Fort Lewis College’s Red Mountain Project records completion of the wagon-road connection serving Ouray, the Red Mountain district, and Silverton in 1885.

moreHistory: The road carried passengers, supplies, machinery, and ore between Ouray, Ironton, Red Mountain, and regional markets before and alongside the district’s railroad development.
